scope: Director review scheduling and shared API-slot ownership. No fresh complete-story benchmark; forecast inputs and cost calibrations unchanged.

changes.directorReview: After complete storyboard assembly and full cadence validation, each independent factual group can proceed through full review, optional repair and exact recheck without waiting for unrelated groups. Ordered facts/state and whole-chapter acceptance remain required. Custom/serial providers retain their serial path.
changes.apiSlots: Each existing network attempt owns one of the same four shared slots through response collection and receipt retention/settlement. Cache lookup, preparation and budget wait happen outside the slot; validation, timing persistence and cache publication complete after release.
preserved: Exact request bodies, models, reasoning, output limits, image/reference bytes, reference order and check/repair coverage.
Distinct request ownership, durable receipts, UNKNOWN liabilities, original retry eligibility, stale-source checks and atomic acceptance.
No slot increase, new automatic replay, reduced checks or new production GPU.

historicalReplay.scope: Saved two-chapter current-calibration request durations, replayed without new inference or API contention. This is not a fresh performance measurement.
limits: The repaired group is already the slowest initial review, so independent chains remove no API-duration barrier in this trace.

The readiness project's earlier saved 61m02 reference used eight-slot history versus four saved slots and a different review version. Other selected projects/manual scenarios can display different estimates.
The earlier 52m31 theoretical floor is an aggregate planner abstraction, not a proven physical capacity floor.

offline.scope: 48 completed-response replays over 12 frozen images in baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline order, with five outer workers and four shared API slots. Real private project/trace/performance/ledger/cache writes; no artificial delays or model/network latency.
offline.elapsedScope: Mean twelve-check arm wall time. The replay showed no overall batch-time gain.
offline.candidateZeroTailInterpretation: Settlement and release occurred in the same measured clock tick; zero recorded is not a claim of truly zero execution time.
limits: Offline replay has zero network/reasoning latency and cannot establish paid API throughput.
Twelve images from one source, two repeats per implementation; ABBA reduces drift but is not a statistical guarantee.
Project, trace, performance, cache and ledger durable writes are real private writes with no artificial sleeps.
API slot scope changes; external record_timing/store/performance implementation is held constant.

apiPilot.scope: Twelve frozen images, QC adapter + real durable record_timing + cache writes only; excludes full video, image generation, repair, voice and render.
apiPilot.elapsedScope: Mean twelve-check arm wall time, two arms per version in ABBA order.
apiPilot.latencyAttributionLimit: Baseline mean wire/response time was 16.5202 seconds per check versus 13.3666 seconds for the candidate. This accounts for most of the observed batch gap; the 18.6 percent shorter mean cannot be attributed to the slot change or extrapolated to complete production.
apiPilot.candidateZeroTailInterpretation: Settlement and slot release occurred in the same measured clock tick, not truly zero execution time.

qualityComparison.interpretation: Stochastic repeated reviews of the same 12 unique images, two repeats per version. Findings vary; these are not 48 independent quality cases and do not establish repair efficacy or equivalent returned findings.

limits: Only twelve frozen images from one source and two repeats per version. ABBA reduces drift but supplies no causal speed guarantee.
QC adapter plus real durable private timing/cache work only; image generation, repair, voice, render and complete-story production were excluded.
No new automatic replay, model/reasoning/tier change, reference reduction or slot-cap increase.

backend.scope: Selected director, QC, overlap, budget, journal, store and profile integration. Synthetic API streams.

validation.scope: Regression and source validation are complete. Installation/publication verification is separate; these tests do not measure full-story throughput.

budget.basis: 48 paid API dispatches settled at $0.01676422, with zero retries, reserved balance or unresolved requests. This is within the existing $0.15 pilot subcap and shared $2 allowance. Prior conservative GPU/disk accounting includes setup/warmup and is counted once. No new GPU/storage spend.

interpretation: The direct measured benefit is removal of post-settlement validation/persistence/cache work from scarce API-slot ownership; the work still completes before the caller returns.
The real pilot had an 18.6 percent shorter mean batch, but different wire/model latency explains most of the gap; no causal throughput or complete-story speedup is established.
The offline replay showed no batch-time gain, and the current historical director trace has zero chain-only saving.
All current forecast inputs, duration/cost calibrations and the 12.3-minute voice estimate stay unchanged.
